jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

Wealth Planning \& Advice is a group of experts in trusts \& estates, tax planning, financial planning and planning in related areas for individuals and their entities (operating businesses, private foundations, etc.). Our role is to work with advisors and their clients to educate them about wealth planning opportunities both simple (e.g., asset titling, beneficiary designations) and complex (e.g., GRATs, split\-interest trusts). We provide intellectual capital to clients across the wealth continuum and will work one\-on\-one with clients in appropriate circumstances. Familiarity with the taxation of entities and of estates and trusts is also useful but not required. Knowledge of issues relating to securities\-based compensation (restricted stock, employee stock options, performance share units, etc.), pre\-liquidity planning, and concentrated position management (such as 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds) will also be a plus.


As the Executive Director, Wealth Planner within J.P. Morgan Wealth Management, you will leverage your deep understanding of tax and trust \& estate laws to communicate complex information in a simple, non\-technical manner to both clients and advisors, as well as field leadership. You will adopt a goal\-oriented approach when engaging with clients, which involves familiarizing yourself with the various investment, banking, and lending products and platforms available to our advisors across J.P. Morgan Wealth Management. This knowledge will enable you to identify issues and opportunities for client engagement. Additionally, you will collaborate with field management to develop regional strategies and provide guidance on their execution. A natural curiosity for people, planning, and the wealth management industry, along with independent initiative and responsiveness, are essential qualities for success in this role.


**Job Responsibilities:**


* Work with divisional leadership and WP\&A leadership to develop and present content across different wealth management topics.
* Serve as a resource to the JPMWM field in the areas of both simple and sophisticated tax and trust \& estate planning strategies as well as in concentrated position management, corporate executive services, and pre\-liquidity transaction planning.
* Partner with field leadership and Practice Management to integrate estate and tax planning concepts into goals\-based advice.
* Maintain up\-to\-date knowledge of both federal and state tax laws relating to our areas of focus.
* Promote J.P. Morgan's knowledge and sophistication to outside centers of influence, primarily accountants and attorneys.
* Work with Advisors to develop business opportunities with new and existing clients.
* Provide unbiased comprehensive and customized wealth planning advice to clients and prospective clients.
* Work with individuals across the entire wealth spectrum and have experience with tax and wealth transfer strategies.
* Actively participate in team discussions to proactively propose planning ideas and industry trends that can be shared with the field.
* Travel to local and out of state branches, as needed.

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills:**


* 4\-year college degree and either J.D, LLB, CPA or CFP
* 7 plus years of practice as a trusts \& estates lawyer, tax advisor, or financial planner
* Knowledge of issues relating to securities\-based compensation (restricted stock, employee stock options, performance share units, etc.), pre\-liquidity planning, and concentrated position management (such as 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds.
* Must be comfortable working with individuals across the entire wealth spectrum and have experience with tax and wealth transfer strategies; familiarity with financial planning, investments, and corporate executive issues.
* Ability to drive business results with broad background in trust and estate planning issues.
* A strong self\-motivated individual who can work closely with Advisors without daily contact with a direct manager.
* Strong presentation skills in one\-on\-one and group meetings
* Experience and ability in understanding clients' financial situations and personal circumstances
* Must be able to coach colleagues, Financial Advisors and clients (very strong partnership skills)
* Individual with high ethical standards who never sacrifices integrity and works in the clients' best interest

**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills:**


* Series 7 \& 66 required (may be fulfilled within 4 months of assuming role)
* Familiarity with financial planning, investments, corporate executive issues and concentrated stock management is a plus
* 10b5\-1 plans, derivative\-based transactions, and exchange funds, and concentrated stock management is a plus
* Experience with financial planning software a plus

FEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE ACT:


This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase's review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.


**ABOUT US**  

  

  

Chase is a leading financial services firm, helping nearly half of America's households and small businesses achieve their financial goals through a broad range of financial products. Our mission is to create engaged, lifelong relationships and put our customers at the heart of everything we do. We also help small businesses, nonprofits and cities grow, delivering solutions to solve all their financial needs.


We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. **About the Organization**


Heal the Bay is the most recognized environmental nonprofit group in LA for a reason: we have been keeping Southern California's coastal waters and watersheds safe, healthy, and clean for people and marine life since 1985\. Using education, science, advocacy, and community action, we raise awareness and make progress with practical solutions to often complex problems. We conduct hundreds of beach and community cleanups each year, informing people about the root causes of pollution along the shorelines and in their neighborhoods. We advocate for strict water quality regulations that protect the health of both humans and the animals that call local creeks, rivers, and the Santa Monica Bay home. We operate the award\-winning Heal the Bay Aquarium at the Santa Monica Pier, inspiring visitors to become stewards for the region’s most important natural resource: clean water. We also educate and inspire the next generation of environmental stewards, with more than 10,000 students joining us each year for school field trips, science\-based classroom presentations, and events. Learn more about us at www.healthebay.org/our\-impact

**About the Role**


The Science \& Policy Director is a key leadership role at Heal the Bay, responsible for advancing our mission of making coastal waters and watersheds in Greater Los Angeles safe, healthy, and clean.


Reporting to the CEO, the Director manages a team of scientists and policy experts to drive strategic goals, with a focus on inland and coastal water quality, biodiversity, climate change and environmental justice. Specifically, Heal the Bay’s current strategic science and policy priorities include:

* **Clean Water \& Public Health** – Protecting the health of people and coastal waters by reducing urban runoff, stormwater, wastewater, nutrients, and other sources of pollution; advancing stormwater capture and watershed solutions; providing trusted water\-quality information; and serving as a watchdog for water\-quality regulations and NPDES permits.
* **Marine Ecosystem Protection \& Restoration** – Protecting and restoring healthy marine ecosystems and biodiversity through science, policy, MPAs, responsible resource management, and applied conservation and restorative aquaculture. Oversee Heal the Bay’s conservation and restorative aquaculture work at the Aquarium/Research \& Discovery Center, ensuring projects are scientifically rigorous, mission\-aligned, and connected to broader restoration and policy priorities.
* **Climate \& Coastal Resilience** – Integrating climate change into Heal the Bay’s science and policy priorities and advancing solutions that strengthen the resilience of coastal and watershed ecosystems and Greater Los Angeles communities.
* **Pollution Prevention** – Reducing plastics, DDT and other legacy contaminants, and emerging and industrial pollutants through science\-based policy, advocacy, source reduction, and systems change.
* **Science\-Based Response to Emerging \& Acute Threats** – Helping Heal the Bay identify and respond appropriately to emerging or acute threats to coastal ecosystems and public health, including sewage releases, oil spills, wildfires, and other significant pollution events.


Key responsibilities include working with the CEO to develop the overall strategic vision for achieving Heal the Bay’s science and policy goals. Independently, the Director is responsible for developing advocacy campaigns, overseeing research and regulatory analyses, and representing Heal the Bay in public forums. The Director also manages relationships with policymakers in Los Angeles and Sacramento and collaborates with external partners.


Candidates should have a strong background in environmental policy and science, with expertise in one or more of the following areas: water quality, ocean and coastal policy, climate change and its impacts on Los Angeles’ coastline, and environmental justice. The ideal candidate will have at least five years of experience leading a team.


Heal the Bay offers a dynamic, mission\-driven environment where science, education, community action, and advocacy are at the core of our work.

	+ **Track and analyze** policies, regulations, and legislation at regional and state levels.

**GHJ is looking for a** **High Net Worth (HNW) Tax Managing Director**


**WHY we get up in the morning**



At GHJ, we foster a flexible, entrepreneurial environment so our people achieve their personal and professional goals.



Our success is driven by retaining the best, diverse talent. We invest in our people and technology to deepen firm expertise and fuel sustainable growth. And we partner with our clients locally and globally to deliver innovative solutions.


**WHAT we believe**



GHJ works side by side with business leaders and nonprofit organizations to deliver responsive, high\-impact advisory, tax and accounting solutions that drive real results. Headquartered in Los Angeles with offices in Buffalo, Denver, Orange County and San Jose and backed by our own dispersed workforce, GHJ meets clients where they are to help leaders achieve their strategic goals.


**THRIVING On Our Own Terms**



We are deeply committed to our core values of Bright Minds, Brave Hearts and Bold Actions and incorporate them into every aspect of our business. By living these values, GHJ measures success by the strength of our relationships, the quality of our impact and the integrity of our actions. The Firm’s independence allows us to make strategic choices to innovate, invest and evolve with purpose. Ultimately, GHJ values operational excellence, financial discipline and the courage to prioritize sustainability over size.


**Summary of Role:**

GHJ is seeking an accomplished High Net Worth (HNW) Tax professional with deep experience in serving high net worth individuals and their related entities.



This position reports to the Tax Department Practice Leader.



The Tax HNW Managing Director will be responsible for leading client engagements requiring individual, trust and gift tax expertise. The ideal candidate will have advanced technical skills in a variety of tax areas, along with well\-developed and demonstrated management and supervisory skills. Administrative, leadership, and business development responsibilities are also key elements for this position.


### **You will be responsible for:**



The Tax HNW Managing Director is responsible for the efficient, accurate, complete, and timely preparation of all clients' tax returns whether prepared personally or by supervision of others. Advanced technical skills in a variety of tax and accounting areas, along with well\-developed and applied management and supervisory skills, are required. Responsibilities include:


* Managing the preparation and review of individual, trust and gift tax returns for high net worth individuals and their families;
* Performing technical tax review and approval of all tax returns of any complexity;
* Participating in client meetings and tax planning efforts for a variety of clients;
* Acting as a resource for tax preparers/specialists on specific tax issues and/or questions;
* Communicating to the appropriate firm personnel important tax and tax developments affecting the firm's clients;
* Managing governmental tax examinations; may represent the client before the appropriate taxing authorities;
* Supervising tax staff and providing on\-the\-job training;
* Working to develop responsible, trained staff by assisting in recruiting, performance evaluations, developing training aids, and acting as an instructor in professional development programs;
* Maintaining a knowledge of general economic and political trends of possible tax or other legislation that could affect the business climate;
* Participating in firm's practice development efforts through involvement with referral sources, community and industry activities.
### **What we need from you:**


* 10\+ years of experience in public accounting (tax), demonstrating a proven ability in handling tax complexity, scope, and research.
* Prior leadership of client engagements and supervisory experience of managers and staff.
* Required exposure to Forms 1040 (Individual return), 1041 (trust return), 1065 (partnership/LLC return), 1120S (S corporation return), and 709 (gift return).
* Experience with forms 5227 (Split Interest Trust Information return) and 706 (Estate return) would be a plus.
* Excellent oral \& written communication skills.
* Self\-starter with the ability to work independently and use good judgment.
* Strong interpersonal skills
* Creative thinker with entrepreneurial approach to client interactions, including tax planning and bringing value to clients.
* Willingness to lead firm or tax department initiatives and be seen as a leader in the tax department.
### **What skills \& experience you’ll bring to us:**


* Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business, or related equivalent.
* Masters of Science degree in Taxation or a J.D. highly preferred
* CPA certification or active law license required.


**Seven decades, one enduring focus: our people and our clients.**



GHJ is a national independent advisory, tax and accounting firm that partners with businesses and nonprofit organizations to deliver clarity and confidence. Since 1953, GHJ has combined deep industry expertise with an entrepreneurial spirit to help leaders achieve their strategic goals.



GHJ is headquartered in Los Angeles and serves clients nationwide, backed by its own dispersed workforce. With nearly 300 professionals and 25\+ partners, the Firm provides senior\-level expertise with deep industry capabilities in food and beverage, media and advertising, entertainment and nonprofit.



GHJ is a top\-ranking firm in the U.S. and member of HLB International. Through this global network, GHJ offers seamless access to resources in over 150 countries while remaining fiercely focused on client success.

Brooklyn Defender Services (BDS) seeks a Director of Operations and Facilities.


BDS is a public defense office representing low\-income New Yorkers in criminal, family, immigration, and civil legal matters. BDS has 750\+ employees with multiple locations in Brooklyn and Queens in New York City. Our work with clients is focused on the intersection of the legal systems that disproportionately impact Black and Brown people living below the poverty level in Brooklyn and Queens.


BDS represents thousands of people each year who have diverse, complex, and multi\-faceted legal needs. In addition to a zealous legal defense, our interdisciplinary teams of attorneys, social workers and advocates provide a wide range of legal and advocacy services, including in the areas of housing, public benefits, education, and employment. BDS staff work collaboratively and across disciplines to deliver high\-quality legal services that serve the people we represent, their families and communities.


The Director of Facilities is responsible for the strategic planning, day\-to\-day operations, and continuous improvement of all facilities\-related functions across the organization. This role ensures that physical spaces are safe, functional, compliant, and aligned with organizational needs, while delivering a high\-quality workplace infrastructure for staff and visitors.


The role combines operational leadership, facilities planning, vendor management and cross\-functional collaboration to maintain and enhance workplace infrastructure.

**Responsibilities**

* Oversee all facilities operations.
* Supervise Operations Staff.
* Prepare and keep up on budget for facilities and operational needs.
* Approve invoices, track spending trends, and implement cost\-control strategies.
* Lead RFP processes, contract negotiations, and performance evaluations for vendors related to facilities and operations.
* Ensure all vendors meet service level agreements, compliance standards, and cost expectations.
* Emergency preparedness.
* Respond to urgent issues and coordinate rapid resolution of facility\-related incidents.
* Partner with the Chief Operating Officer and other leadership to align facilities strategy with organizational growth and programmatic needs.
* Project management of facilities and operational issues as they arise.
* At the current time, BDS is renovating a new space that is on track to be completed in late 2027\-2028\. The Director of Facilities will be involved in tracking progress and implementing the new space when it comes online.

**Qualifications**

* 7–10\+ years of facilities or operations management experience.
* Demonstrated experience managing multi\-site facilities.
* Knowledge of building systems, safety regulations, and compliance requirements.
* Proven ability to manage budgets and drive cost efficiencies.
* Experience in nonprofit, legal services, or mission\-driven organizations preferred.
* Prior experience with a large renovation a plus.

**Key Competencies**

* Strategic and operational leadership.
* Strong project management skills.
* Problem\-solving and decision\-making under pressure.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management.
* Attention to detail with a service\-oriented mindset.
* Ability to balance long\-term planning with day\-to\-day operational demands.

**Position Information**


This is a full\-time, exempt, salaried position. The normal schedule is Monday to Friday 9am\-5pm. The position is based at BDS’s offices in Brooklyn and Queens, with regular travel between office locations as needed. The role also may require after\-hours availability for emergencies or major facilities projects.


BDS determines salary on a pay scale based on education and experience. For this position there is a salary range of $125,000\-$150,000\. For someone with extensive experience, it is possible BDS would consider additional salary. BDS offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance and a 403(b)\-retirement plan. To support work/life balance and family\-friendly policies, BDS has generous vacation, sick, holiday, family, and medical leave policies.

**Application Instructions**


Click “Apply Now” to submit a cover letter and resume.


Please submit your application by**October 30, 2026\.**

*Brooklyn Defender Services is a proud equal opportunity employer committed to celebrating diversity and maintaining an equitable and inclusive work environment. We strongly encourage candidates of all identities, expressions, orientations, disabilities, and experiences to apply. If you require an accommodation due to a disability or another reason, please contact the Managing Director of Human Resources, Christina Wallace, at* *cwallace @ bds.org**.*

Executive Director \- Care Net Pregnancy Center  

  

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive and ministry leader of Care Net Pregnancy Center of Indian River County. As an ambassador of Jesus Christ, the Executive Director provides Christ\-centered leadership and oversees the organization's people, programs, finances, operations, development, and community relationships.


**Mission:**

To connect with and empower women and men facing an unplanned pregnancy with free, immediate


transformational support to choose life for their unborn child and discover abundant life in Christ.


**Vision:**

To be a transformational Christian refuge.


**QUALIFICATIONS**

Demonstrates a personal and growing relationship with Jesus Christ and a commitment to Christian ministry.


Fully supports Care Net's Statement of Faith, Statement of Principle, Mission, Vision, Core Values, and life\-affirming ministry.


Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent leadership experience preferred.


Demonstrated leadership experience, preferably in a Christian nonprofit, ministry, pregnancy center, healthcare, family\-support, or community\-service organization.


Experience supervising and developing staff and leading organizational operations.


Experience with budgeting, financial oversight, fundraising, donor development, and community relationships.


Strong strategic thinking, organizational, interpersonal, communication, writing, and public\-speaking skills.


Demonstrates sound judgment, initiative, flexibility, problem\-solving ability, confidentiality, emotional maturity, integrity, and a strong work ethic.


Proficient in technology and organizational management systems.


**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1\. CHRIST\-CENTERED MINISTRY LEADERSHIP**

Demonstrate a personal and growing relationship with Jesus Christ and model Christ\-centered servant leadership.


Champion Care Net's Mission, Vision, Core Values, Statement of Faith, and life\-affirming ministry.


Provide spiritual leadership, encouragement, prayer, and direction to staff and volunteers.


Foster a culture of compassion, dignity, grace, integrity, accountability, and excellence.


Ensure Care Net's Christian identity is reflected throughout its programs, services, communications, and relationships.


**2\. STRATEGIC \& ORGANIZATIONAL LEADERSHIP**

Translate strategic priorities into annual goals, measurable objectives, and departmental plans.


Evaluate organizational and ministry effectiveness using appropriate data and outcomes.


Ensure staffing, programs, finances, technology, and resources are aligned with the organization's Mission and strategic priorities.


Identify opportunities, challenges, risks, and emerging needs that will affect the future of Care Net.


**3\. BOARD RELATIONSHIP \& ACCOUNTABILITY**

Serve as the primary staff liaison to the Board of Directors.


Maintain a transparent, collaborative, and accountable relationship with the Board.


Attend Board meetings and provide timely reports regarding ministry impact, finances, staffing, operations, development, and strategic progress.


Implement Board\-approved policies, budgets, priorities, and strategic direction.


Maintain a clear distinction between Board governance and staff operational responsibilities.


**4\. STAFF \& VOLUNTEER LEADERSHIP**

Recruit, supervise, develop, evaluate, and retain qualified staff who support Care Net's Mission and Christian values.


Establish clear responsibilities, expectations, goals, and accountability.


Provide leadership development, training, encouragement, and appropriate correction.


Facilitate regular staff and leadership meetings that promote communication, prayer, teamwork, problem\-solving, and accountability.


Ensure volunteers are appropriately recruited, trained, supported, and equipped for ministry.

**5\. MINISTRY PROGRAMS \& PATIENT/CLIENT IMPACT**

Provide oversight of revenues, expenditures, financial controls, restricted funds, and resource allocation.


Ensure accurate financial and organizational records and timely reporting to the Board.


Oversee day\-to\-day operations, policies, procedures, facilities, technology, data systems, and administrative infrastructure.


Ensure appropriate confidentiality, compliance, risk management, and internal controls.


Model faithful stewardship, transparency, integrity, and accountability in the use of all resources entrusted to Care Net.


**7\. FUND DEVELOPMENT \& DONOR RELATIONSHIPS**

Provide leadership for Care Net's annual development and fundraising strategy.


Cultivate and steward relationships with donors, churches, foundations, businesses, and community partners.

**Lead the Next Era of Tropical Agricultural Research**

**The Hawaiʻi Agriculture Research Center (HARC)** seeks an entrepreneurial, collaborative, scientific executive to lead the organization through a pivotal period of transition and into its next era of growth and impact. Building on more than a century of applied agricultural research in Hawaiʻi, HARC has repeatedly evolved with Hawaiʻi agriculture, from its origins serving the sugar industry to a diversified nonprofit research organization. Today, HARC has an opportunity to again define how its scientific capabilities, facilities, partnerships, and distinctive tropical setting can address the changing needs of agriculture in Hawaiʻi and beyond.

**About HARC**

HARC is a private 501(c)(3\) nonprofit agricultural research organization headquartered at the Kunia Research Station in Waipahu, Oʻahu. Its team of scientists, agronomists, foresters, conservationists, and technical experts works across five core research divisions. Current work includes crop improvement and breeding, coffee leaf rust resistance, agrivoltaics, native forest restoration, crop propagation and tissue culture, and applied research supporting Hawaiʻi producers and natural\-resource managers.

**The Opportunity**

HARC is at an institutional inflection point. The organization seeks a leader who respects and learns from its history and deep institutional knowledge while recognizing that agricultural science, crop biotechnology, research funding, technology, and Hawaiʻi’s agricultural economy continue to change. The next Executive Director will help HARC consolidate a compelling mission and long\-term vision, establish a focused and financially sustainable research strategy, and build organizational alignment around that direction.

**This is a CEO\-level opportunity for a leader who can unite** scientific credibility, organizational leadership, financial and operational discipline, and external partnership development with the vision and energy to help shape HARC’s future. Following more than three decades of continuity in executive leadership, the next Executive Director will work collaboratively with HARC’s senior project leaders, staff, Board, producers, community partners, funders, industry, universities, and government agencies to clarify strategic direction, focus research priorities, strengthen financial sustainability, and position HARC for its next chapter.

**Key Responsibilities**

● **Organizational leadership, mission \& strategy:** Lead a collaborative process with the Board, senior project leaders, staff, and key partners to refine HARC’s mission, establish a compelling long\-term vision, set research and organizational priorities, and translate them into measurable plans and outcomes.

● **Financial sustainability \& business development:** Build a durable financial model by aligning resources with strategic priorities, strengthening existing programs, diversifying federal, state, philanthropic, industry, and fee\-for\-service revenue, and developing new sponsored\-research and partnership opportunities.

● **Research portfolio \& scientific innovation:** Work with HARC’s scientific leaders to evaluate and focus the research portfolio, support high\-quality applied research, identify opportunities in new crops and emerging technologies, and help develop competitive grants, contracts, collaborations, and programs with meaningful producer and community impact.

● **People, culture \& organizational alignment:** Build a high\-performing, collaborative organization by developing and retaining strong staff, clarifying roles and expectations, fostering accountability and professional growth, and aligning personnel and resources with HARC’s strategic priorities. Make difficult organizational decisions when needed while communicating them fairly, respectfully, and transparently.

● **Operations \& infrastructure:** Provide executive oversight of budgets, contracts, compliance, research facilities, farms,

laboratories, and organizational systems; ensure projects meet commitments and deliverables.

● **External relations \& partnership development:** Serve as a visible ambassador for HARC and deepen relationships with Hawaiʻi producers, communities, industry, universities, government agencies, and funders while developing national and international partnerships that advance tropical agricultural research and innovation.

**The Candidate We Seek**

The strongest candidate may come from a nonprofit research institute, agricultural or biotechnology company, university research center, government research organization, agricultural technology company, public\-private partnership, or another science\-based organization. Prior service with the title Executive Director or CEO is valuable but is not required. HARC is interested in demonstrated executive capacity and increasing responsibility.

**Required Qualifications**

● Advanced degree in agriculture, plant science, natural resources, biological sciences, or a closely related field; a PhD or equivalent

advanced scientific training is required.

UVC is seeking its next Chief Executive Officer to lead the organization's continued growth and impact. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will be responsible for UVC's strategy, fundraising, external relationships, team, and financial sustainability. This is a highly external, entrepreneurial role for someone who can build relationships, raise resources, connect people, and identify opportunities to strengthen entrepreneurship across Upstate New York.


*Prior nonprofit experience is not required. Experience as a founder, investor, business leader, fundraiser, or ecosystem builder may be equally relevant.*

**About UVC**  

Founded in 2010 by entrepreneurs, Upstate Venture Connect (UVC) is a 501c3 nonprofit working to build a more connected, entrepreneur\-led economy across Upstate New York. UVC supports founders building high\-growth, venture\-backable companies by helping them access the relationships, experience, capital, customers, talent, and other resources they need to scale while remaining in the region.


UVC serves as the connective tissue among Upstate New York’s regional startup communities. Our Founder Network is free to join and provides entrepreneurs with personalized introductions to other founders, investors, experienced operators, mentors, advisors, corporate partners, and potential customers. UVC is tracking more than 800 high\-growth companies across Upstate NY and facilitates more than 550 curated introductions for them every year. Its broader network includes more than 18,000 contacts and startup supporters. (More info: UVC 2025 Annual Report)


UVC’s Community Advocate network provides a locally based presence across Upstate New York. Community Advocates act as regional connectors, scouts, and champions. They identify and engage founders, organize local gatherings, build partnerships, make strategic introductions, and connect entrepreneurs in their communities to UVC’s nationwide network. This model allows UVC to strengthen individual startup communities while connecting founders to opportunities beyond their immediate region.


At the center of UVC is the UNY50 Leadership Network, an invitation\-only group of accomplished entrepreneurs, executives, and business leaders committed to giving back. UNY50 members volunteer their time, experience, and networks to help emerging founders navigate the challenges of building and scaling companies. The majority are also active early\-stage investors.


UVC hosts more than 20 curated events per year. Its programming centers on four types of gatherings: regional Office Hours, which give founders access to personalized feedback from UNY50 members, investors, and mentors; multi\-day Founder Roadshows, which connect select Upstate companies with investors, customers, and entrepreneurial networks in major markets like NYC, Boston and Washington, DC; curated founder and leadership dinners, designed to build trusted relationships among experienced and emerging entrepreneurs; and Unleashed, UVC’s annual invitation\-only founders retreat. These programs create opportunities for meaningful connections that can help founders access capital, customers, talent, mentorship, and other resources needed to scale.


UVC’s work is funded through foundation support, corporate sponsorships, individual donations, and program revenue. Its impact is also made possible by a statewide community of corporate and community partners, universities, financial institutions, investors, board members, advisors, volunteers, and founders who share a commitment to creating more high\-growth opportunities in Upstate New York. (UVC Partners)

**Key Responsibilities**

* Fundraising \& Growth: Own UVC's fundraising and revenue strategy with a goal towards long term financial sustainability. Build and maintain relationships with corporations, foundations, financial institutions, government partners, donors, and sponsors.

* Ecosystem Leadership: Serve as a visible ambassador for UVC and Upstate NY’s entrepreneurial community; grow and engage the regionwide network, and connect founders to capital, customers, talent, mentors, and other opportunities.
* Strategy, Operations \& Leadership: Set organizational priorities with the Board and lead their execution. Develop and oversee the annual budget that balances strategic goals with the resources available to the organization. Manage UVC's team and financial resources to support the strategy and stay compliant with regulatory requirements. Oversee the Community Advocate network and execution of UVC's programs and gatherings, and identify new opportunities for partnerships, programs, and growth.

* A strong affinity for UVC's mission and entrepreneurship in Upstate New York
* Demonstrated success building relationships, partnerships, and networks
* Experience fundraising, generating revenue, developing and managing to a budget, selling, or securing financial support from individual donors, corporate sponsors, foundations and/or government sources
* An entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to move between strategy and hands\-on execution
* Credibility with founders, investors, business leaders, funders, and community partners
* Strong communication and public speaking skills
* Comfort with emerging tech including use of AI
* Experience leading a team, managing a budget, and driving organizational priorities


This position has a base salary of $110,000\-$130,000 plus opportunity for incentive compensation

We offer a comprehensive suite of benefits including health insurance coverage and 401K savings accounts.

Founded in 1946, BoysGirls Clubs of Whatcom County (BGCWC) has been a cornerstone of youth development in our community for 80 years. Today, we operate four Clubhouses and four licensed Early Learning Centers, serving young people and families across Whatcom County.

**Job Title:** Advancement Director, West
**Department:** Advancement
**Location:** Remote (preferred within the Pacific Northwest)

This position requires an ability to travel.
**Reports To:** Managing Director, Major Gifts, West  


**Context**: At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees.  


**Scope:** This is an opportunity to join the Advancement team of the country’s leading grassroots environmental organization. At a critical time for the planet, Sierra Club is running highly effective campaigns to address climate change, protect wilderness and wildlife, and advance these priorities by rooting the work in justice and equity for all. We are seeking an Advancement Director responsible for identifying, cultivating, and soliciting gifts of $25,000 and greater. In this position, you will be part of a dynamic team of gift officers raising upwards of $65 million dollars annually for our high\-impact campaigns from individual donors, family foundations, and institutional funders within the defined geographic region. The Advancement Director will engage donors and prospects throughout the region via discovery, cultivation, engagement, solicitation and stewardship activities. Valid driver’s license, satisfactory driving record, and proof of auto insurance required. 40\-50% of travel is typically expected in this role.
### **Job activities include but are not limited to:**



* **Portfolio Management**
	+ Personally manages a portfolio of high\-potential prospects and donors by identifying and cultivating new prospects.
	+ Engages with prospects and donors through face\-to\-face meetings, phone, video conference, digital engagements, and writing based on a clear strategy for cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
	+ Solicits assigned donors for gifts of $25,000 and more to meet organizational priorities and annual projected fundraising revenue goals.
	+ In collaboration with the Sr. Managing Director, Chief Advancement Officer (CAO) and other Advancement Team members, identifies and pursues new prospects, developing and implementing a clear strategy for each prospect, leading to new and increased giving over time by connecting donor philanthropic priorities with Sierra Club’s programs and priorities.
	+ Leverages donor engagement events in the West and Northwest geographic regions to identify, cultivate and solicit new and existing prospects and donors.
	+ Prepares and sends donor correspondence, including written solicitations and proposals.
	+ Develops and maintains an in\-depth knowledge of the organization’s activities, priorities and needs. Applies this knowledge in matching the interests and needs of prospective donors with the strategic needs of the organization and campaigns.
	+ Captures all interactions and relationships in the donor database in a timely manner. 30%\-40% travel is likely for this role with travel occurring across the country.
* **Strategic Planning and Execution**
	+ Drives strategies and plans to identify, cultivate, upgrade and/or solicit new donors, with an eye towards building a strong pipeline of qualified major donors and high\-net\-worth individuals with the capacity to give $25,000 or greater.
	+ Maintain knowledge and expertise in environmental issues broadly, including climate change, clean energy, land, water and wildlife conservation. Work with Campaign and Chapter key staff and teams to help develop and implement relevant major gift programs, initiatives, events, and materials.
### **The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:**


* Senior\-level, extensive experience, equivalent combination of experience and education in development and major gift fundraising, including a strong background in the identification, qualification and cultivation and solicitation of six and higher figure gifts to nonprofit organizations or similar equivalent experience.
* Proven ability and inclination to build a portfolio of prospects and grow a revenue pipeline through active identification, qualification and cultivation strategies
* Strong knowledge of fundraising best practices, planned giving, financial and/or estate planning concepts, and campaign planning.
* Personal success identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding individual and institutional donors at the major and principal gifts levels, and ability to inspire high\-net\-worth individuals and institutional funders to provide significant financial support to an organization.
* Deep understanding of and appreciation for the philanthropic process and individual giving behaviors.
* Experience working with organizational leadership, preferably in a non\-profit setting.
* Ability to develop strong, positive, and constructive relationships with internal and external stakeholders; high emotional intelligence and flexibility, with the ability to continually experiment, learn, and revise strategies; and the exceptional ability to juggle a heavy volume of div
